papers.title: V-CoLA: Vision Token Compression with Linear Attention
papers.problem: Vision-language models waste compute on image tokens, and old compression tricks fail on the newer linear-attention models.
papers.fix: V-CoLA keeps 99.5% of original accuracy with half the image tokens and runs prefill 1.86 to 6.15 times faster.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you run image-heavy models, you can cut cost sharply, so test token compression before buying more hardware.
papers.limitation: The shown tests use benchmark sets, so real workloads may lose more accuracy at high compression.

papers.title: Self-Retrospection Distillation: Turning Post-hoc Experiences into Prior Foresight
papers.problem: Agents trained with reward-only learning get no signal when every attempt in a group earns the same reward.
papers.fix: Self-Retrospection Distillation lifted a 2B agent from 0.0% to 60.6% success where plain reward training stalled.
papers.practicalUseCase: If your agent fails every try, learning from finished attempts can still help, so add it before giving up.
papers.limitation: Gains reach 24.2 points on 10 tasks, so results on your own tasks may be smaller.

papers.title: Real Long-Term Memory for AI: A 50-Million-Token Window That Is Faster and Cheaper Than Recompute
papers.problem: Language models forget text outside their context window and recompute stored state every time you send a prompt.
papers.fix: Loading saved blocks from disk ran 2.8 to 4.3 times faster and used 8.8 to 12.3 times less GPU energy.
papers.practicalUseCase: If this holds, long chat memory gets cheap, so consider disk-backed caching for apps that reread big documents.
papers.limitation: It reuses stored state rather than widening attention, and the store needs terabytes of local disk.

papers.title: AgentGarten: Code Worlds for Evolving Agents
papers.problem: Agents learn only what their practice worlds teach, and faithful, realistic worlds are hard to build.
papers.fix: AgentGarten lets agents learn in 4 rounds, where a conventional reinforcement learning agent needs millions.
papers.practicalUseCase: If this holds, you can train agents in code-built worlds quickly, so try a simulator before collecting real data.
papers.limitation: The shown gain comes from the authors' own tests, not from outside replication.

papers.title: LongTake: Learning to Sustain Dynamics in Long-Horizon Video Generation
papers.problem: AI video makers drift into near-static scenes and lose picture quality when clips run past a few seconds.
papers.fix: LongTake training gives more motion than short-clip training on 30-second videos at similar visual quality.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you build video tools, train on long real clips, because short clips teach the model too little about motion.
papers.limitation: The excerpt gives no exact scores, and results cover only 30-second and 60-second videos.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks form sustainability committees, but it was unclear whether those committees change real environmental results in Islamic banks.
papers.fix: A sustainability committee lifts overall environmental scores and resource reduction in Islamic banks, but not green products or innovation.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you judge an Islamic bank's green claims, look past its committee and check for actual products.
papers.limitation: The study covers emerging markets with both bank types, so findings may not fit other regions.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Sustainability sukuk are growing fast, but nobody had mapped how they are issued or what sets their size.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 issuances from 2012 to 2022, sukuk backed by equity-based contracts, strong security, and social goals came out larger.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you track green sukuk, expect growth mostly in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Saudi Arabia, so watch those markets first.
papers.limitation: Data end in 2022, and the study shows links between features and issue size, not cause.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan lacked clear evidence that AI and big data tools raise competitiveness and sustainable development.
papers.fix: AI use, big data skills, and data management all link positively to bank competitiveness and sustainable development performance.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you work in Islamic banking, invest in data skills and systems, because they link to better results.
papers.limitation: A one-time survey of 214 managers in Jordan shows links, not cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks in dual systems lacked clear evidence on which national factors drive their growth.
papers.fix: Across 218 banks in 12 countries, ICT adoption is the strongest growth driver, and high-tech exports help only alongside ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you plan bank growth, fund digital systems first, because exports and rules alone do little.
papers.limitation: The data cover 218 banks in 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, so other places may differ.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Many Muslim-majority countries still exclude people from finance, even though Islamic finance has grown for a decade.
papers.fix: In 35 OIC and OECD countries, income, tertiary education, institutions, internet access, and age mix drive inclusion in OIC states.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you shape OIC policy, spend on digital networks, youth, women, and income growth, because those move inclusion most.
papers.limitation: The study covers 35 countries from 2005 to 2021, so single countries may behave differently.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students face constant exams and peer comparison, and nobody knew how often they feel like frauds.
papers.fix: Impostor feelings were frequent among medical students before licensing, with results varying by sampling method and region.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you train or study in a high-pressure field, expect impostor feelings and treat them as common, not personal failure.
papers.limitation: Pooled results vary a lot between studies, so treat any single figure with care.

papers.title: Psychometric properties of the Arabic Perceived Digital Well-Being Scale (PDWS) in Saudi young adults
papers.institution: Imam Mohammad ibn Saud Islamic University
papers.problem: Research on young adults and screens mostly tracks harm, with few tools to measure whether their digital life feels good.
papers.fix: The Arabic Perceived Digital Well-Being Scale proved a reliable and valid measure in Saudi young adults aged 18 to 25.
papers.practicalUseCase: To check your screen habits, ask how they affect your life, not only how long you scroll.
papers.limitation: Participants joined online in Riyadh, and the one-time design cannot show cause.
